findings.title: Arroyo commit callback invoked from background thread
findings.body: `_commit_loop` calls `commit_function` from a separate daemon thread. Arroyo's `Commit` callable is not thread-safe and is meant to be called from the main thread, typically inside `poll()`/`submit()`. Calling it concurrently with the StreamProcessor's own loop can race on its internal state. Committable offsets should be computed and committed inside `poll()` instead.

findings.title: Shared queue pool shut down on partition revocation
findings.body: The `FixedQueuePool` is created once per factory and shared by every strategy that `create_with_partitions` returns. On a rebalance, arroyo calls `close()`/`join()` on the old strategy, which shuts down the shared pool's queues and workers. The next strategy then reuses that dead pool, and any `put` on it raises `ShutDown`. The consumer stops processing after the first rebalance.

findings.title: join() drops in-flight work and its final commit
findings.body: `join()` sets the shutdown event and stops the commit thread before the queues are drained. Each worker's `shutdown` flag is also set, so the `while not self.shutdown` loop exits after the current item even though `q.shutdown(immediate=False)` alone would let it drain. As a result, queued items may never be processed, and offsets that were completed are never committed. After a rebalance this causes reprocessing, and work can be lost if another consumer has already committed past those offsets. The `timeout` argument is also ignored.

findings.title: Unbounded queues, no backpressure
findings.body: Each `queue.Queue()` is created without a `maxsize`, and `submit` never raises `MessageRejected`. The docstring claims natural backpressure, but a slow worker lets memory grow without limit while the consumer keeps polling.

findings.title: Offset tracker state leaks across revoked partitions
findings.body: Offsets for revoked partitions are never cleared from the tracker. If a partition is reassigned later, the stale `last_committed`/`all_offsets` state remains. A rewind to a lower offset would then never be committed, and stale entries for other partitions can still be committed after they are revoked.

findings.title: queue.ShutDown requires Python 3.13
findings.body: `queue.ShutDown` and `Queue.shutdown()` only exist in Python 3.13 and later. On older interpreters the `except queue.ShutDown` clause raises `AttributeError` when it is evaluated, and `shutdown()` fails; the exception is caught and only logged. Workers then block in `get()` forever.
